identification.summary: UTA0352 is Volexity's tracking designation for a suspected Russia-linked cluster that abuses legitimate Microsoft OAuth 2.0 sign-in workflows to phish Microsoft 365 accounts. Volexity reported it alongside a second cluster, UTA0355, in an April 2025 report [S1][S2][S3]. Contact begins over Signal or WhatsApp with a message impersonating European political officials or Ukrainian diplomats and an invitation to a private meeting about Ukraine [S2][S4]. The lure leads to a genuine Microsoft login page, and the victim is persuaded to pass an authorization code back to the actor, which gives access to Microsoft Graph data such as email and files [S2][S4][S5].
identification.firstObserved: Volexity reported activity since early March 2025 for UTA0352 and UTA0355 combined [S2][S3]; the report was published 2025-04-22 [S6].
identification.notes: Volexity names (UTA = unattributed threat actor) are vendor cluster labels; Microsoft has no mapped name in this record. Sources disagree on which cluster (UTA0352 or UTA0355) used a compromised Ukrainian government account; do not attribute it to UTA0352 without the primary report [S2][S4].

attribution.confidence: Volexity assesses with medium confidence that the actors behind UTA0352 and UTA0355 are Russian [S2][S3]. No government attribution found.
attribution.basis: Volexity cites targeting aligned with Russian interests (Ukraine-related individuals and organizations) and similarity to tactics seen in a February 2025 campaign [S3][S6]. The primary Volexity report was not opened; basis is taken from secondary coverage of it.

objectives: Gain access to Microsoft 365 accounts (email and files via Microsoft Graph) of people connected to Ukraine, human rights and related work, consistent with intelligence collection [S2][S3][S4]. Collection intent is inferred from the access obtained; no source states it explicitly.

sectors: Individuals historically associated with Russia-related threat activity (per Volexity, medium confidence)
regions: Ukraine and Europe (lures impersonate officials of European countries and Ukraine) [S2][S4]
targeting.notes: Targets are described as people tied to Ukraine and human rights work [S3]. Specific victim organizations are not named in the secondary sources gathered. Sector list reflects the combined UTA0352/UTA0355 reporting and the record's imported summary; per-cluster splits are not confirmed.

capabilities.summary: Social engineering over Signal and WhatsApp with impersonation of European and Ukrainian officials [S2][S4]. Links open a legitimate Microsoft OAuth sign-in that ends at an in-browser Visual Studio Code page (insiders.vscode.dev) showing an authorization code the victim is told to send back [S4][S5]. The actor exchanges the code for an access token to Microsoft Graph, reportedly valid for up to 60 days per secondary coverage [S2][S4]. Imported record text also cites lookalike URLs imitating a Romanian government authentication system and targeting of Microsoft Teams [S6][S7]; these details were not confirmed in the primary report. Volexity-suggested detections include OAuth sign-ins using the Visual Studio Code client ID, redirects to vscode-redirect.azurewebsites.net, new devices registered from proxy IPs, and unexpected MFA prompts [S3]. Device registration to Entra ID for persistence was described in the UTA0355 case [S3]; one secondary source describes it generally [S5]. No custom malware is reported.

diamond.adversary: Suspected Russia-linked cluster tracked by Volexity as UTA0352, medium confidence.
diamond.capability: Signal/WhatsApp social engineering, OAuth 2.0 authorization-code phishing via a legitimate Microsoft login and VS Code redirect, Microsoft Graph access [S2][S4][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Lookalike or redirect URLs including the Visual Studio Code in-browser redirect; indicator vscode-redirect.azurewebsites.net [S3]; lookalike URL imitating a Romanian government authentication service per imported record [S6].
diamond.victim: Individuals and organizations tied to Ukraine and human rights work [S3][S4].
diamond.socioPolitical: Aligned with Russian interests in the Ukraine conflict; collection against aid, policy and rights communities [S3][S6].
diamond.technology: Microsoft 365 / Entra ID OAuth 2.0 flows with permissive first-party client IDs, and consumer messaging apps outside enterprise monitoring [S3][S4].

gaps: The primary Volexity report could not be opened (WebFetch host resolution failed); all details come from secondary coverage and search snippets.
Which of UTA0352 or UTA0355 used the compromised Ukrainian government account is inconsistently reported [S2][S4].
Microsoft Teams targeting and the Romanian-government lookalike URL come from Malpedia/Strobes profile summaries and were not confirmed in primary text [S6][S7].
No Microsoft name, government attribution, named victims, or infrastructure list beyond a few indicators was found.
Activity after April 2025 was not identified in the sources gathered.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the Microsoft 365 / Entra ID tenant and the personal messaging accounts (Signal, WhatsApp) of staff who interact with Ukraine or coalition partners [S2][S4]. STEP 2: The actor needs no malware or exploit; a valid user click and code relay yields Graph access, so user behavior and tenant OAuth policy are the decisive terrain [S4][S5]. STEP 3: Template is a messaging-app approach impersonating an official, a genuine Microsoft login, code hand-back, token use, and possible device registration [S3][S4]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued credential and token phishing of Ukraine-linked civil-society and policy staff. MDCOA is the same approach aimed at coalition or DoD-adjacent personnel through personal devices, with Entra device registration providing persistence. Candidate indicators: OAuth sign-ins using the Visual Studio Code client ID, redirects to vscode-redirect.azurewebsites.net, new device registrations from proxy IPs, and unexpected MFA prompts [S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: feed Entra sign-in and device-registration logs into cyber defense monitoring using Volexity's suggested indicators [S3]. (2) Authorities: personal-device messaging and user training fall under command policy rather than network-defense authorities; coordinate with the responsible information-system owner. (3) Mission assurance: restrict or require approval for OAuth and device-code flows and consent to first-party client IDs where not needed, and plan for token revocation. (4) Coordination: share indicators with partner and DIB defenders; treat Volexity labels as vendor clusters and do not merge them with other named actors absent further evidence.

provenance.importedSummary: UTA0352 is a Russian threat actor attributed to phishing campaigns that exploit Microsoft OAuth 2.0 authentication workflows, often impersonating government officials to lure targets into providing sensitive information. The actor has been observed using malicious URLs disguised as legitimate services, such as a Romanian government authentication system. UTA0352 has also targeted Microsoft Teams and employed social engineering tactics via messaging platforms like Signal and WhatsApp. Volexity assesses with medium confidence that UTA0352 is involved in operations themed around Ukraine, targeting individuals and organizations historically associated with Russian threat activities.
